thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT - elevated p99 decode latency detected in us-west clusters for streaming routes. SLO monitor fired at 11:42 UTC. Affected endpoints: /v1/generate-stream, /v1/chat/stream.

lia (oncall): I'm on it. p95 jumped from ~120ms to ~260ms, p99 up to ~2.2s on streaming. Marking P1 and paging eng-runtime + eng-sre.

matt (eng-runtime): Noted. Recent deploys: TRT/FlashAttn runtime kernel bumped to tag trt-flashattn:3.1 and build image includes new compile flags: `-O3 -march=native -DFAST_KV_ALLOC`. Hypothesis: new kernel + flags change allocator behavior leading to KV-cache growth and host page faults during decode -> tail stalls.

sasha (eng-sre): Looking at node metrics. Rollout reached ~55% of us-west nodes at ~11:10 UTC. Seeing clusters with spikes in minor page faults and long pauses in `copy_kv_cache()` traces.

ryan (prod): Customer impact: intermittent streaming stalls causing a few timed-out requests and degraded UX for some enterprise customers. CS: prepare comms.

lia (oncall): Mitigation options (parallel):
- rollback kernel to previous stable tag on a subset of pools;
- flip runtime env to disable FlashAttention path: `REDWOOD_RUNTIME_DISABLE_FLASHATTN=1`;
- temporarily shift traffic to dedicated clusters that still run older kernel.

matt (eng-runtime): I'll toggle env flag via k8s for streaming runtime: ```kubectl -n infra set env deploy/streaming-runtime REDWOOD_RUNTIME_DISABLE_FLASHATTN=1 && kubectl rollout restart deploy/streaming-runtime``` I'll stage rollout: 10% -> 50% -> 100%.

sasha (eng-sre): I'll trigger kernel rollback using ansible for us-west-1a/1b nodes: ```ansible-playbook -i inventory/us-west rollback-kernel.yml -e image=trt-flashattn:2.9``` Starting first batch now, ETA ~8m. Also cordoning nodes with high pgfault rates.

devops-bot: Event logged: env update started by matt.

lia (oncall): Can we drain nodes showing high minor pagefaults to reduce live tail effects?

sasha (eng-sre): Yes. Will taint and evict in small batches: ```kubectl taint nodes node-uw1b-02 redwood=paging:NoSchedule; kubectl drain node-uw1b-02 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data``` Also adjusting LB to prefer dedicated-backend pool.

matt (eng-runtime): After setting `REDWOOD_RUNTIME_DISABLE_FLASHATTN=1` on 10% of pods, p99 for that cohort dropped from ~2.2s to ~1.3s. Proceeding to 50%.

lia (oncall): Good signal. CS: send immediate notes to flagged enterprise customers, wider notice in 20m.

customer-success: Drafted messages. Notifying direct contacts now. Broader announcement queued. Collecting request IDs.

ryan (prod): Any root cause guesses on why pagefaults spiked? Memory alignment or larger pinned buffers?

matt (eng-runtime): The FlashAttn kernel on 3.1 uses larger pinned allocation for KV caching and changes GPU memory eviction hints. For some host kernels + older NIC firmware, this causes elevated host memory pressure and increased minor faults. I also see higher context switches.

sasha (eng-sre): Correlating firmware versions: nodes with NIC fw-2.1.* show higher pgfault rates. We'll exclude them for now. Recommend firmware upgrades or node replacement.

lia (oncall): Action list:
- matt: finish env-flag rollout to 100% and monitor p95/p99 and error traces.
- sasha: complete rollback for initial node pools, cordon old NIC nodes.
- ryan: compile customer impact list and coordinate credits/comm.
- lia: prepare handoff and runbook for next oncall.

matt (eng-runtime): Env flag at 100%. Observed p99 settle ~600-700ms across impacted endpoints in us-west. CPU usage up ~8% but within headroom. Starting sampling traces for quality check.

sasha (eng-sre): First rollback batch finished; minor pagefaults dropped ~65% on those nodes. LB moved ~35% of traffic to rolled nodes.

lia (oncall): Mitigations stable. We need a durable fix: either adjust kernel allocator defaults or runtime patch to limit pinned KV allocations for FlashAttn. Also add rollout gating on node pgfault signals.

matt (eng-runtime): I'll file an RFC for a conservative allocation mode and a tenant-scoped opt-out. Opening hotfix PR to make FlashAttn allocation bounds configurable via route metadata.

customer-success: Gathering logs and request IDs. Sent direct notes to two enterprise customers; broader note scheduled in 30m.

lia (oncall): Handoff to tom at 12:30 UTC. Leave incident open; mitigations in place (env disable + partial rollback). Keep watching p95/p99 and streaming stall traces.

devops-bot: Oncall handover initiated: lia -> tom at 12:30 UTC. Checklist incident-1745109999 created.

matt (eng-runtime): Notes for tom: traces in `gs://redwood-logs/prod/streaming/17451*`, trace id prefix `decode-tail-17451`. RCA ticket INFRA-4521.

sasha (eng-sre): Follow-ups: run NIC firmware inventory for us-west; schedule updates for fw-2.1.*. Add rollout gating rule for kernel images based on pgfault threshold.

lia (oncall): Closing handoff. Please add action items to postmortem ticket and react when done.

matt (eng-runtime): :white_check_mark: RFC and PR opened.

sasha (eng-sre): :white_check_mark: rollback runbook executed and infra follow-ups filed.

customer-success: :white_check_mark: outreach done. Broader notice queued.

incident-bot: Severity changed P1 -> P2 at 12:05 UTC after mitigations.

lia (oncall): Assign postmortem owners: matt (runtime), sasha (sre), ryan (prod). Add timeline and customer impact.

(END)
